action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:64); sodium 133 mEq/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies normal or negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up (blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, serum anti-GluN1 cell-based assay read with the CSF)
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, infectious and thyroid causes of the new encephalopathy and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which supports but cannot replace the CSF assay.

action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Compares with the HSV admission to separate HSV relapse from a new process and excludes structural causes before LP; MRI does not confirm the antibody diagnosis.

action_criteria.rationale: A negative HSV PCR excludes HSV relapse and the CSF cell-based anti-GluN1 assay establishes post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

action_criteria.rationale: Tumors are uncommon in men and post-HSV disease is not tumor-associated, so a scrotal ultrasound is a sufficient screen; tumor removal would be part of first-line treatment.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1 to 2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Restart IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours (in place of oral valacyclovir) until CSF HSV PCR excludes HSV relapse, then stop.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Scrotal ultrasound shows no tumor; no further tumor imaging is needed unless the course is atypical or refractory.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication: seizures continue on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, so increase the levetiracetam dose or add lacosamide; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation, insomnia and catatonia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

accepted: Post-herpes simplex virus anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis

differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1 and HSV-2 PCR negative; new bilateral MRI signal without restricted diffusion, hemorrhage or enhancement; new chorea and orofacial dyskinesias; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, GABA-A)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, GABA-A) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.
Electrographic seizures of both temporal lobes, extreme delta brush, chorea and orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic lability and CSF pleocytosis with new oligoclonal bands.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced encephalopathy or neuroleptic malignant syndrome (including levetiracetam behavioral effects)
differential.key_features: Urine drug screen negative; no antipsychotic exposure; CK 290 U/L; levetiracetam level in range, and its behavioral effects do not explain chorea, seizures or CSF inflammation.

key_clinical_evidence: Ten days of apathy, then confusion, paraphasic speech, chorea and orofacial dyskinesias, catatonic posturing, focal and generalized seizures and labile blood pressure 6 weeks after HSV-1 encephalitis: five of the six Graus 2016 groups.

CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:256) on cell-based assay with a negative CSF HSV PCR: definite post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016, Armangue 2018); serum positive 1:64 is read with the CSF.

MRI shows new bilateral medial temporal FLAIR signal beyond the chronic left HSV change without restricted diffusion or hemorrhage; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds and here mainly separates a new process from HSV relapse.
EEG shows extreme delta brush and seizures of both temporal lobes; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Scrotal ultrasound is normal; post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis is not tumor-associated (Armangue 2018).
Earlier immunotherapy is associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: About a quarter of patients develop autoimmune encephalitis within about 3 months of HSV encephalitis, most with NMDAR antibodies (Armangue 2018); a negative CSF HSV PCR and new choreoathetosis point to the autoimmune process, and acyclovir is given only until PCR excludes relapse.
red_herrings.data_point: Recent HSV-1 encephalitis and the treating team's working hypothesis of HSV relapse.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on HSV relapse and antiviral therapy alone, delaying antibody testing and immunotherapy.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome needs antipsychotic exposure, a markedly raised CK and lead-pipe rigidity; he has had no antipsychotic, and this mild CK rise is explained by seizures and dyskinesias.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias, low-grade fever and increased tone.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure 16 cmH2O. Lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 32 cells/uL, 88% lymphocytes), protein 48 mg/dL and normal glucose (62 mg/dL, CSF/serum ratio 0.63). Six CSF-specific oligoclonal bands, none on the previous sample; IgG index 0.82 (elevated). Gram stain: no organisms; bacterial culture: no growth at 48 hours. HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV and enterovirus PCR not detected. Anti-NMDA receptor (GluN1) IgG positive on cell-based assay, titer 1:256. Clinical correlation recommended.

contraindications: Class warning: haloperidol and other high-potency dopamine D2 antagonists are associated with severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic malignant-like reactions in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
Documented aspirin urticaria: avoid aspirin and NSAIDs that cross-react through COX-1 inhibition; paracetamol is an alternative for fever or pain.
interactions: Valacyclovir (current, 1 g three times daily) with IV acyclovir: the same drug (valacyclovir is the acyclovir prodrug); do not give both, stop valacyclovir while IV acyclovir is given.
Acyclovir IV: crystal nephropathy risk; maintain hydration and monitor creatinine.
Levetiracetam (current): no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction with corticosteroids, IVIG, acyclovir, lorazepam or lacosamide; renally cleared.
IVIG: risk of renal impairment and thrombosis; ensure hydration and avoid rapid infusion rates.
High-dose methylprednisolone: hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypokalemia; monitor glucose and electrolytes.
Lorazepam with other sedatives: additive respiratory depression.
general.summary: Current levetiracetam and valacyclovir reviewed against the acute agents; valacyclovir duplicates IV acyclovir. Class cautions listed above.

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: 27% of patients with HSV encephalitis developed autoimmune encephalitis, 64% of them with NMDAR antibodies, typically within about 2 months; these cases were not tumor-associated.
results.source: Armangue T et al. Lancet Neurol 2018;17:760-772

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDAR encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

clinical_pearls: Autoimmune encephalitis developed in 27% of HSV encephalitis patients, 64% of them with NMDAR antibodies, usually within about 2 months (Armangue 2018).
A negative CSF HSV PCR separates post-HSV autoimmune encephalitis from HSV relapse.
New choreoathetosis or orofacial dyskinesias after HSV encephalitis should prompt CSF NMDAR antibody testing.
New MRI signal beyond the original HSV territory without new restricted diffusion or hemorrhage favors the autoimmune process.
Post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis is not tumor-associated.
metadata.diagnostic_challenge: Post-HSV NMDAR encephalitis presenting 6 weeks after treated HSV encephalitis. The initial treating team assumes HSV relapse, but negative HSV PCR, new bilateral MRI changes beyond the original HSV territory, extreme delta brush on EEG, and characteristic movement disorder all point to autoimmune encephalitis requiring immunotherapy rather than antivirals.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required tools, 3 red herrings, subtype=P; requires CSF antibody confirmation + MRI/EEG/labs synthesis; severe multistage syndrome demanding ICU-level care and earlier second-line escalation
metadata.revision_reason: Independent Reviewer 2 anti-NMDAR audit: tumor screening tailored by age/sex and moved out of lab payloads; paired serum/CSF anti-GluN1 reachable; routine EEG baseline with selected continuous escalation; blanket CAP CT, FDG-PET and blood cultures removed

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Carlos Reyes is a 28-year-old right-handed Hispanic man who presents to the emergency department with recurrent confusion, new involuntary movements, and a witnessed seizure, occurring 6 weeks after treatment for confirmed HSV-1 encephalitis. Six weeks ago, he was hospitalized at General Hospital for 18 days with HSV-1 encephalitis — presenting with acute confusion, fever, and left temporal lobe involvement on MRI. CSF HSV-1 PCR was positive. He was treated with 21 days of IV acyclovir and had a good recovery, with mild residual word-finding difficulty that was improving at outpatient follow-up. He was started on levetiracetam for seizure prophylaxis (had one seizure during the acute illness) and valacyclovir for maintenance antiviral therapy. He returned to light teaching duties 2 weeks ago and was doing well per his wife — oriented, independent in daily activities, and cognitively much improved. Over the past 10 days, his wife has noticed progressive personality changes. He became apathetic, stopped initiating conversation, and lost interest in activities. Then 5 days ago, he became irritable, suspicious, and confused — asking repetitive questions and getting lost in their apartment. Three days ago, she noticed new involuntary movements — his hands and arms would make flowing, dance-like movements (chorea), and he began making repetitive lip-smacking and chewing movements. Yesterday, she witnessed a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds. She called 911 and he was brought to the ED. His wife is extremely concerned and states 'he was getting better and now it is worse than before.' The initial treating team's working hypothesis is HSV encephalitis relapse and they plan to restart IV acyclovir.

neurological_exam.additional: Two brief staring episodes observed during the 30-minute examination — each lasting approximately 20-30 seconds with behavioral arrest, orofacial automatisms (lip smacking), and subtle left arm posturing. Patient unaware of these episodes afterward. Autonomic instability present: blood pressure fluctuating between 120/74 and 148/92, heart rate ranging from 78 to 118 bpm. Temperature 37.8°C. Wife confirms these movements (chorea, lip smacking) and staring episodes are entirely new — they were NOT present during the prior HSV encephalitis hospitalization or during recovery.
neurological_exam.coordination: Unable to reliably assess — choreiform movements and inattention preclude formal testing.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal 3 mm, reactive to light bilaterally. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. No papilledema. Visual fields full to confrontation. Prominent orofacial dyskinesias — intermittent lip smacking, chewing movements, and tongue protrusion every 15-30 seconds. These are NEW movements not present during the prior HSV hospitalization. Facial sensation intact. Facial strength symmetric. Hearing intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline.
neurological_exam.gait: Unsteady, wide-based. Requires assistance to ambulate. Unable to perform tandem gait.
neurological_exam.mental_status: GCS 13 (E3V4M6). Confused, disoriented to date and place (thinks he is at a different hospital). Affect is flat with intermittent unprovoked agitation. Speech is fluent but with frequent paraphasic errors and tangential responses. Unable to perform serial sevens. Registration 3/3, recall 0/3 at five minutes. His wife reports this is a dramatic change from 5 days ago, when he was oriented and functional at work.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral choreiform movements of the upper extremities — involuntary, irregular, flowing movements affecting hands and forearms bilaterally. These are also NEW. Intermittent catatonic posturing — arms held in fixed elevated position for 10-20 seconds when stimulated. Strength is grossly 5/5 in all extremities when patient cooperates. Tone mildly increased in bilateral upper extremities.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ symmetric bilaterally. Plantar responses extensor bilaterally (Babinski positive bilaterally).
neurological_exam.sensory: Inconsistent responses — patient unable to cooperate reliably with sensory testing.
